answers.core:
1. Variadic parameters affect how functions are defined and called. This is a syntax-level capability, like match, yield, or await. You can’t simulate true variadic behavior with an add-on, you can only work around it with clunky wrappers or array-passing conventions.

2. Built-in functions like print() already support variadic arguments. But developers can’t replicate that behavior in their own APIs. This creates an inconsistency between core and user-defined functions.

3. An asset library can’t modify how the parser interprets function signatures. You can’t define func log(...) or intercept native argument handling from an add-on. At best, you can offer a helper like logv(["a", "b"]), which still requires awkward syntax and breaks intuitive usage.

This isn’t a niche feature, it could benefit mostly any project that uses multiple arguments of an undetermined amount.
answers.workaround:
Yes, it can technically be worked around, but the workaround is clunky and undermines the clarity and elegance that variadic parameters offer.

Currently, developers must either:

    a) Wrap arguments manually in an array: console.log(["Item:", key])

    b) Define multiple optional parameters: func log(a, b := "", c := "", ...)
